messages:
incidentbot: AUTOPAGE fired for node=gpu-host-07 (tenant-zone-a). Alert: kubelet NotReady + kernel OOPS + gpu driver fail. pager: https://pd.example/INC12345 :rotating_light:
PagerDuty: Alert triggered, routing to oncall (Maya).
Maya: acked. I'm on it. pulling serial output now.
Maya: quick check — any customer-facing routes on this node? @Jordan can you confirm?
Jordan: checking now — metrics show a spike in 95th latency for /generate for tenant org-42 starting ~12:04UTC. ~3% of requests retried. Might be traffic that was routed to this rack.
Raj: thanks. Maya, if kubelet is NotReady we should cordon and drain to avoid pod thrash. If this is kernel OOPS we might need RMA.
Maya: running: kubectl get node gpu-host-07 -o wide
Maya: output:
```
NAME          STATUS     ROLES   AGE     VERSION
gpu-host-07   NotReady   <none>  42d     v1.28.2
```
Maya: starting serial console capture, tailing /var/log/kern.log for OOPS patterns.
Kelly: I see recent kernel message on the host: "GPU: tdr_detected: Xid 79" then a stack trace and then "kernel: Kernel panic - not syncing" around the same time.
Maya: paste of last few dmesg lines:
```
[  312.345678] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00:00): 79, 0x00000020, 0x00000000
[  312.345689] kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 0000000000000010
[  312.345695] kernel: kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception
[  312.345700] reboot: Restarting system
```
Maya: host did a soft-reboot after panic. kubelet has flapped.
Sam: were GPU-using pods pinned to this host? Any stateful that need special eviction?
Maya: two pods with local ephemeral data: model-cache-sync-1 and heavy-train-spot-77. Both are non-critical for a few minutes; model-cache sync can be rebuilt from S3.
Raj: plan: 1) mark node unschedulable (cordon) 2) try graceful drain with --delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets 3) if drain stuck, force evict 4) switch traffic via routing policies to spare pool.
Maya: cordoning now: kubectl cordon gpu-host-07 -> node/gpu-host-07 cordoned
Maya: starting drain: kubectl drain gpu-host-07 --force --delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets --timeout=10m 
Maya: drain progress: evicted 8 pods, 2 in CrashLoopBackOff blocking, forcing eviction.
Kelly: ops note: NVMe SMART on this host looks okay. Hardware counters show GPU ECC errors increasing before the panic. Could be driver/firmware or thermal.
Jordan: customer impact update: org-42 support ticket incoming; overall platform error rate bumped 0.6% last 10m. No other tenants showing problems.
PagerDuty: Escalation to secondary oncall (Raj) due to high-severity and hardware hint.
Raj: joined. Maya — do we have a live serial log capture on the second boot? Might help know if panic is deterministic.
Maya: serial logs show boot kernel oops early in NV driver init on reboot 2. Attaching snippet: 
```
[    5.123456] nvidia: probe of 0000:03:00.0 failed with error -5
[    5.123467] nvidia: GPU device not responding
[    5.123480] Kernel panic - not syncing: Attempted to kill init!
```
Maya: I initiated a cold power-cycle from OOB, host is back to POST and failing later in nv driver init.
Raj: escalation decision: leave node cordoned, mark for RMA if hardware continues to fail boot, and remove from rotation permanently for now. We'll also kick a Dedicated pool fallback for tenants using this rack.
Sam: can we automatically reroute active sessions? Are there sticky session pins?
Maya: routing tier has per-tenant affinity, but fallback rules allow a warm pool. I triggered a failover for org-42 to dedicated-warm-02. Confirmed new requests route there.
Jordan: org-42 support updated: they saw ~6 failed requests and 4 retries. Customer-facing latency normalized after 30s of failover. Filing a post-incident note.
Kelly: followups: capture nv driver version, kernel config, and GPU firmware. I'll collect `nvidia-smi -q` from host image (if up) and cross-check with fleet baseline.
Maya: collecting: driver=525.105.17, kernel=5.15.0-rc, firmware=13.0.2.
Raj: good. Also check kernel modules dmesg timestamps and any memory cgroup OOMs.
Maya: I see no container OOMs before the panic. Looks like device fault.
PagerDuty: Incident severity set to Sev2 (hardware causing production retries).
Maya: I'm going to open an infra ticket and tag hw-rma. Also adding entries for the console capture to the incident doc: https://redwood.example/incidents/INC12345-doc
Maya: handing off to Raj for longer-running followup. Raj, you take lead on RMA and fleet sweep?
Raj: taking lead. I'll schedule a maintenance window to repro with earlier driver, and if persistent file RMA. Also will run a constrained test on host image in staging to reproduce.
Sam: noted — I'll update the routing policy to lower affinity thresholds for the rack to reduce single-host blast radius.
Jordan: will draft the customer blurb for org-42 and SRE postmortem checklist.
Maya: thanks team. I'll keep socket open for any urgent ask, but moving to monitoring for other hosts in rack. :thumbsup: 
Raj: marking this thread for follow-ups: collect driver/fw, rma ticket #RMA-742, fleet sweep plan, routing policy change PR.
Jordan: last update for now — org-42 support notified, they accepted transient failure explanation, asked for root cause and ETA.
Maya: last check: no other nodes showing the same kernel oops pattern in the rack. Leaving node cordoned and flagged. Closing active pager but keeping incident doc live.
incidentbot: AUTOPAGE cleared for INC12345 (ack by Maya).
Maya: closing thread, transferring to eng-infra backlog.
